citeAs: Hauret, J., Olivier, M., Langrenne, C., Poirée, S., & Bavu, É. (2024). vibravox (revision 071945b). Hugging Face. https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cnam-LMSSC/vibravox
creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu (Conservatoire national des arts et métiers; French-German Research Institute of Saint-Louis)
description: Vibravox is a French speech dataset of audio recordings captured simultaneously with five body-conduction audio sensors and one airborne reference microphone. It contains about 45 hours per sensor from 188 participants under quiet and noisy acoustic conditions, with recording-condition annotations and linguistic transcriptions including phonetic transcriptions.
name: Vibravox
publisher: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam) / Laboratoire de Mécanique des Structures et des Systèmes Couplés (LMSSC)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Participants were deliberately recruited to form a diverse and gender-balanced group. The released dataset includes 97 female and 91 male speakers; Appendix A reports age statistics with female mean age 25.9 years (median 22, range 19–59), male mean age 31.4 years (median 27, range 18–82), and overall mean age 28.55 years (median 25, range 18–82).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Post-processing quality control used automatic filters based on phoneme error rate from Whisper alignments, SNR between speech and silence, and a speech-level-vs-sensor-baseline check. Samples with PER > 10%, SNR ≤ 1.5 dB, or Lspeech50 not exceeding baseline silence level were discarded.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Participants read sentences sourced from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Text was normalized by lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes, then converted to IPA phonetic transcriptions with the CoML lab phonemizer; manual phonetic transcription was added for words the phonemizer did not recognize. Recording-condition annotations and linguistic transcriptions are included.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that existing body-conduction speech datasets are limited in scale, language coverage, sensor diversity, and noise scenarios, and they designed Vibravox to address these gaps. They also deliberately recruited a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants to improve representativeness and inclusivity.
rai:dataCollection: Data were collected from participants wearing six simultaneously recorded sensors: five body-conduction sensors and one airborne reference microphone. Each participant completed four consecutive recording phases: reading speech in quiet, remaining silent in noisy conditions, remaining silent in quiet, and speaking in noisy conditions created with a 56-loudspeaker 3D spatialization setup.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper discusses data inconsistencies and missing or unusable observations during collection, including mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from their initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, and cases where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped. After post-processing, 12 of 200 participants were excluded and only 28,471 of 30,568 speech-clean sentences were retained.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of 6-channel audio recorded simultaneously at 48 kHz and 32-bit resolution from a headset microphone, forehead accelerometer, soft in-ear microphone, rigid in-ear microphone, throat microphone, and temple vibration pickup, plus associated text transcriptions, phonetic transcriptions, and recording-condition annotations.
rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Direct measurement, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that Vibravox is not the largest BCM dataset. It also reports remaining issues such as occasional insertion defects or poor acoustic sealing for in-ear microphones, participant-specific sensor fit variability, and that post-processing excluded 6% of participants and 6.8% of pronounced sentences to support rigorous comparison rather than maximizing data volume.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset includes post-filtering to retain only correctly pronounced and sufficiently high-SNR speech-clean utterances. Accepted samples had voice-activity timestamps extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, with 15 ms trimming when adjusted boundaries exceeded the original audio limits. The released dataset is then split by speaker into train, validation, and test sets with 80%/10%/10% of male and female speakers.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each acquisition channel during recording. Text from French Wikipedia/Common Voice was filtered to remove most proper names, numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors, then normalized by lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes. Audio post-processing further filtered utterances using Whisper-based alignment, phoneme error rate, silence/speech level statistics, and SNR criteria.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support development of robust communication systems in noisy real-world settings, with applications mentioned in military operations, industrial environments, access control, intelligence gathering, and monitoring vital signs such as heart rate. The paper emphasizes privacy protection under GDPR and hopes the release will drive progress in body-conducted speech analysis.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use cases include speech enhancement or bandwidth extension, speech-to-phonemes or automatic speech recognition, speaker verification, robust communication in noisy environments, voice commands, and monitoring vital signs such as heart rate using speechless-clean recordings.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: The annotation and filtering pipeline used whisper-timestamped, a speech-to-text engine based on Whisper with dynamic time warping for word timestamps and vocalization alignment, and the CoML lab phonemizer to generate IPA phonetic transcriptions.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains voice recordings from human participants and associated speaker attributes including gender balance and age statistics; the paper also notes physiological sounds in speechless recordings that may support heart-rate or breathing analysis. The dataset is described as GDPR-compliant, with informed consent, anonymization, and encryption during storage and analysis.

null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: paper describes filtering, trimming, and augmentation for experiments, but no imputation or fill-in of missing dataset values
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: no versioning, update cadence, or maintenance commitment described beyond public release
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no external annotation platform such as MTurk, Prolific, or Label Studio mentioned
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: paper describes recording durations per participant and release year, but gives no calendar dates or collection period for when data were gathered
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: paper does not report multiple independent annotations per item or a numeric count of annotators per item; it only indicates retained transcriptions and phonetic transcriptions
